title: Pre-Qualification Letter Age at a Homesite Reservation Extension
content:
**What decides the extension letter shortening on a Homesite Reservation hold extension?**
The age of the pre-qualification letter on the extension date, counted in calendar days from the date printed on the letter, as on the reservation record, to today.

**What are the bands?**
The extension letter shortening is **2** days where the letter is more than **60** days old, **1** day where it is more than **45** but no more than 60 days old, and zero where it is 45 days old or less.

**Is a letter exactly 60 days old in the higher band?**
No. At 60 days the letter is more than 45 but no more than 60 days old, so the shortening is 1 day; at 61 days it is 2 days.

**And at exactly 45 days?**
The letter is 45 days old or less, so there is no shortening; at 46 days the shortening is 1 day.

**Which date is the letter date?**
The date printed on the pre-qualification letter recorded on the reservation.

**Example (hypothetical).** A letter dated 1 March, extension taken on 1 May: the age is 61 days (30 days to 31 March, then 31 days to 1 May), so the shortening is 2 days.
